question: Should a character's life carry health insurance and medical costs, and if so what are they? For an adult by age, job type and state: whether they are insured and how (employer, marketplace, Medicaid, Medicare, uninsured), the typical monthly premium and yearly out-of-pocket cost, and what an acute or serious illness costs someone insured versus uninsured.
requestedBy: How the world changes thread, answering lamontae's 2026-09-22 11:40 a.m. ET question about where the healthcare numbers come from: the game shows none.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Illness has recovery times only (placeholders), no cost.
Monthly living costs list rent, food, utilities and other necessities; no medical line.

sourcesChecked.source: AHRQ MEPS-IC Research Findings54, 2024 private-sector employer health insurance
sourcesChecked.whatItSettled: Public aggregate benchmark; territory/place-specific gaps documented.

title: What medical costs and insurance an ordinary person faces
usableAnswer: A design decision (should medical costs exist in play) and, if yes, sourced national figures (KFF, CMS, MEPS) with how they vary by state and age.
whyItMatters: Healthcare is a major political issue in the game, but a character never pays for or is insured against anything medical.

findings.estimate: MEPS-IC2024 supplies total and employee premiums by firm size; CE2024 supplies household healthcare spending with SE. Use employee contribution for household payroll deductions and employer contribution in employer books; never charge total premium twice.
findings.mechanism: Insurance status, plan premium/deductible/copay/out-of-pocket maximum and actual medical episode determine cash cost. Premiums and care prices must not be a single random annual bill.
findings.gaps: No complete age/job/state/territory joint cost table or source-supported universal episode price extracted. ACS coverage and MEPS-HC age/condition expenditure tables are further needed; do not fabricate exact local medical rates.
